name: B10-0562/2025 – Motion for a resolution
title: MOTION FOR A RESOLUTION on the draft Commission Implementing Decision of renewing the authorisation for the placing on the market of products containing, consisting of or produced from genetically modified maize NK603 pursuant to Regulation (EC) No 1829/2003 of the European Parliament and of the Council
part_text:
The European Parliament is asking the European Commission to withdraw its plan to renew the licence for a genetically modified maize called NK603. This maize is engineered to survive spraying with glyphosate, a weedkiller. The Parliament says the safety checks were too narrow, did not look at long-term effects, and that member states never backed the plan with a majority vote. The Parliament also wants the whole way such licences are decided to be reformed.

- **What changes:** Nothing yet. Parliament only asks the Commission to drop the renewal and to propose new rules for deciding on genetically modified crops.
- **Who it affects:** Farmers, food and feed importers, and consumers in the EU, plus the company Bayer, which applied for the renewal.
- **What happens next:** The Commission decides whether to withdraw its plan. Parliament also wants a new law on how these decisions are made.
